policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV opens the verse with a conditional, "Now if we put the horses' bridles into their mouths", which renders εἰ δέ; the RP imperative Ἴδε would have produced "Behold", as ASV in fact writes for ἰδού in v. 4 and v. 5.
εἰς and πρός before the articular infinitive τὸ πείθεσθαι are both purpose constructions rendered alike; ASV's "that they may obey us" reflects either without distinction, and no note is mapped here.
The variation is Greek word order only; English "by rough winds" must place adjective before noun regardless, so ASV cannot distinguish ἀνέμων σκληρῶν from σκληρῶν ἀνέμων.

ASV "whither the impulse of the steersman willeth" does not mark the presence of ἄν or the subjunctive βούληται; "whither" alone carries ὅπου and is equally natural for the generalizing RP form, so no reading is excluded.

The compound μεγαλαυχεῖ and the two-word μεγάλα αὐχεῖ mean the same thing; ASV "boasteth great things" renders either. The mapped note here is an alternative_rendering about ὕλην and does not bear on this unit.

ASV writes the exclamatory correlative "how small a fire", matching ἡλίκον, which pairs with the following ἡλίκην that ASV renders "how much wood" (note: "how great a forest"). RP's ὀλίγον is a plain adjective and yields "a little fire" with no "how".

ASV renders no resumptive "so" or "thus" after "the world of iniquity": "the world of iniquity among our members is the tongue, which defileth...". None of the three alternative_rendering notes supplies οὕτως either, so the RP addition is unrepresented.
The variation is the order of δαμάσαι, δύναται and ἀνθρώπων only; ASV's "the tongue can no man tame" is a fixed English ordering that reflects either arrangement.
ASV "a restless evil" renders ἀκατάστατον (unsettled, restless); ἀκατάσχετον means uncontrollable/unruly and would have given "an unruly evil" as in the earlier English tradition.
ASV "bless we the Lord and Father" renders κύριον; θεόν would have produced "God the Father" — and ASV does write "God" later in the same verse for θεοῦ, showing it distinguishes the two words.

ASV has only the short negative clause "neither can salt water yield sweet", corresponding to οὔτε ἁλυκόν; the RP reading's "οὕτως οὐδεμία πηγή" ("so can no fountain") has no counterpart in the ASV wording.

ASV closes the list asyndetically, "without variance, without hypocrisy", with no conjunction between ἀδιάκριτος and ἀνυπόκριτος, though it renders καί elsewhere in the verse ("mercy and good fruits"). The mapped note glosses ἀδιάκριτος and does not touch the conjunction.

The variant is the Greek article before δικαιοσύνης, which English does not show: "the fruit of righteousness" takes its article from καρπός, and an anarthrous or articular δικαιοσύνης is rendered identically. The mapped note offers "by" for ἐν and does not bear on the article.
